articles.title: FedEx Cup 2026 Points, Playoff Standings After BMW Championship
articles.summary: BMW Championship winner Wyndham Clark, Scottie Scheffler, Rory McIlroy and 27 other golfers are booked for next week's Tour Championship.
articles.body:
BMW Championship winner Wyndham Clark, Scottie Scheffler, Rory McIlroy and 27 other golfers are booked for next week's Tour Championship.

The top 30 golfers in the FedEx Cup standings after Sunday's final round of the BMW Championship are off to East Lake Country Club.

There were three changes in the top 30. All three golfers that moved into the top 30 finished inside the top 10 at Bellerive Country Club.

Full standings can be found here on PGATour.com.

Gary Woodland, Patrick Cantlay and Robert MacIntyre vaulted themselves into the top 30 at the expense of Rickie Fowler, Bud Cauley and Kurt Kitayama.

Woodland was near the top of the leaderboard all weekend. He was one of the co-first-round leaders and ended up in a tie for fourth.

Cantlay had a terrific weekend in terms of the FedEx Cup. His solo second-place finish allowed him to move up 24 positions from 43rd place.

MacIntyre used a five-under 65 on Sunday to move into a tie for seventh place, which came with an 11-spot jump in the standings.

Clark, McIlroy, Collin Morikawa and Chris Gotterup, who were the other golfers in the top four and ties, remained in the top 10 of the FedEx Cup standings.

Clark's victory gave him 750 points and a two-spot move up to third place.

Scheffler enters the Tour Championship with the most FedEx Cup points, but that won't come to his advantage next week.

The Tour Championship format has changed. Now, all 30 golfers will play a straight-up stroke-play event to determine the FedEx Cup winner.

articles.title: BMW Championship: Rory McIlroy third as Wyndham Clark blows big lead before closing out PGA Tour victory
articles.summary: Wyndham Clark claimed a two-shot victory over Patrick Cantlay at the BMW Championship, with Rory McIlroy a shot back in third; Clark let a five-shot lead slip on the final day before claiming a third PGA Tour victory of the season
articles.body:
Wyndham Clark overcame blowing a five-shot lead to edge out Rory McIlroy with a dramatic three-shot victory at the PGA Tour's BMW Championship.

Clark saw his big overnight lead disappear during a thrilling Sunday at Bellerive Country Club, where the US Open champion bogeyed three of his first 10 holes to give hope to McIlroy and the chasing pack.

McIlroy found three birdies in a four-hole stretch around the turn to sit level with Clark heading into the closing stretch, only for his playing partner to post a three-birdie finish to cap off a roller-coaster victory in style.

  • Final BMW Championship leaderboard and other scores
  • Latest PGA Tour news, reports and highlights
  • Get Sky Sports or stream golf with no contract

A level-par 70 was enough for Clark to end the week on 17 under and close out a third PGA Tour victory of the season, following on from the CJ Cup Byron Nelson and the US Open, with Patrick Cantlay claiming solo second to progress through to next week's season-ending Tour Championship.

McIlroy was tied for the lead with three to play but ended four back after a penultimate-hole bogey and Clark's impressive birdie burst, while Gary Woodland, Collin Morikawa and Chris Gotterup shared fourth place.

How Clark held off McIlroy to BMW Championship win

Clark's overnight advantage was immediately cut with a two-shot swing at the first, where he three-putted from 65 feet for bogey as McIlroy holed from 10 feet for birdie.

McIlroy failed to get up and down to save par at the fourth but holed from seven feet to avoid back-to-back bogeys, as Woodland - two groups ahead - made three birdies in his first five holes to get within two.

Clark bogeyed the par-three sixth after a clunky chip from just off the green, with Woodland halving his advantage by birdieing the par-five eighth before inexplicably topping his tee shot into water at the next.

McIlroy made a two-putt birdie at the eighth and picked up a shot at the ninth to reach the turn two back, only to pull level with a birdie at the 11th after Clark had started his back nine with a bogey.

Cantlay also briefly shared the lead until a double-bogey at the 11th, while McIlroy and Clark traded pars to leave the pair tied at the top of the leaderboard with three holes to play.

Clark was birdie-free during the final day until he edged ahead with a 15-footer at the 16th, before adding another at the par-five next - after McIlroy went from bunker to bunker and carded a bogey - to extend his advantage.

Cantlay reduced the lead by birdieing each of his final three holes to set the clubhouse target at 14 under, as Clark closed out his fifth PGA Tour win by pouring in a 15-foot birdie to extend his winning margin.

"As much as I would have loved to have run away with this, it was fun to get the juices going," Cantlay told CBS Sports. "I think it shows that I'm one of the best players in the world. Three wins in one season is my best year yet, coming off my worst year ever and I'm just very pleased with where I am at right now."

On claiming third, McIlroy said: "I'm still not in a spot where I'm super happy with where my game is or where my swing is, so I just have to keep working on it. It's nice to know even when I'm not super happy with everything I can still piece it together and get it around and still give myself a chance to win tournaments."

Morikawa delivered a stunning eagle at the par-five 17th but bogeyed the last to finish on 12 under with Woodland and Gotterup, who carded a final-round 69, as Scotland's Robert MacIntyre extended his season after a five-under 65 lifted him to tied-seventh.

What's next?

The PGA Tour season reaches its climax at the Tour Championship at East Lake GC, where only the top 30 players in the standings are eligible to compete for the FedExCup and $10m first prize.

articles.title: Scottie Scheffler, Rory McIlroy or Matt Fitzpatrick? Have your say on who should win PGA Tour's Player of the Year award
articles.summary: Who will be crowned the 2026 PGA Tour Player of the Year? Have your say! Scottie Scheffler and Rory McIlroy among names who could claim honour; watch all four rounds of the Tour Championship live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
Rory McIlroy insists it’s ‘all to play for’ in the race to be crowned PGA Tour Player of the Year, but who is still in contention for the coveted Jack Nicklaus Award

McIlroy said ahead of the BMW Championship there was 'no chance' he should be considered, despite defending his title at The Masters, but he remains a contender after finishing third behind Wyndham Clark at the BMW Championship.

Scottie Scheffler has won the award - determined by a vote by PGA Tour members - each of the last four seasons and could challenge for a fifth consecutive title, with the world No 1 enjoying another consistent campaign.

  • BMW Championship recap: Final round as it happened
  • Final BMW Championship leaderboard and other scores
  • Latest PGA Tour news, reports and highlights
  • Get Sky Sports or stream golf with no contract

Scheffler, Clark, Matt Fitzpatrick, Chris Gotterup and Cameron Young are all multiple winners on the PGA Tour this season, while others could join to make a late Player of the Year push at the season-ending Tour Championship, live on Sky Sports.

Victory at the FedExCup finale at East Lake this week could be enough to give one of that quintet the edge ahead of the shortlist being revealed in the autumn, with this season's race shaping up as one of the tightest and most open in recent years.

Who will be crowned the 2026 PGA Tour Player of the Year? Take a look at the potential contenders and have your say…

Scottie Scheffler

Scheffler may not have won as many tournaments as he did in 2025, but he has still enjoyed an excellent year, picking up two victories. His first came at The American Express in January, and his second came in August at the FedEx St. Jude Championship.

What's been most remarkable about Scheffler this season is his consistency. The world No 1 has placed as a runner-up five times on the PGA Tour in 2026, notably becoming the first-ever PGA Tour player to secure three consecutive solo runner-up finishes at The Masters, the RBC Heritage and The Cadillac Championship.

Rory McIlroy

McIlroy has won this award three times, and after successfully defending his Masters title in April, he once again finds himself a contender to be crowned the PGA Tour's Player of the Year.

He's played some fantastic golf this season, notably dazzling fans with his incredible distance off the tee at The Open, and has enjoyed some great results too, including a tied-second finish at the Genesis Invitational, top-ten finishes at the PGA Championship and Genesis Scottish Open and, more recently, securing third place at the BMW Championship.

Matt Fitzpatrick

It's been Fitzpatrick's most successful PGA Tour season to date, with the 2022 US Open Champion clinching three PGA Tour victories, while placing as a runner-up twice, notably just missing out on winning The Players.

After being denied by Young at TPC Sawgrass, Fitzpatrick went on to win at his next PGA Tour start at The Valspar Championship, before claiming back-to-back titles at the RBC Heritage and the Zurich Classic of New Orleans alongside his brother Alex.

Wyndham Clark

Clark is another player who has enjoyed his most successful season on the PGA Tour, winning his third event of 2026 at the BMW Championship.

The American's first victory of the year came at the CJ Cup in May, before he won his second US Open title at Shinnecock Hills, with Clark showcasing his incredible putting skills to beat Sam Burns by a shot.

Cameron Young

Young picked up the second and third victories of his PGA Tour career in 2026, winning The Players in March and outscoring Scheffler to win The Cadillac Championship in May.

He came close to winning his first major championship at The Open in July, where he finished one shot back from winner Ryan Fox, in second place.

Chris Gotterup

Gotterup got his 2026 campaign off to a fast start, winning the season-opening Sony Open in Hawaii in January, before he beat Hideki Matsuyama in a play-off to win the WM Phoenix Open the following month.

The 27-year-old's third win came later in the season at the John Deere Classic, making this his most successful season on the PGA Tour yet.

articles.title: LIV Golf League: Bryson DeChambeau, Jon Rahm reflect on uncertain future as Michael La Sasso wins season finale
articles.summary: Michael La Sasso held off Jon Rahm to win LIV Golf Indianapolis; Rahm finished a shot back after a final-round charge at the final event of the season; Bryson DeChambeau discussed the league's long-term future after finishing in tied-third
articles.body:
Bryson DeChambeau insists there’s ‘something fun coming’ and a ‘lot of potential’ in LIV Golf to continue beyond their season finale in Indianapolis.

The 2026 LIV Golf League campaign finished a week early at The Club at Chatham Hills, following the cancellation of the Team Championship, with Michael La Sasso claiming his breakthrough professional victory and Jon Rahm's Legion XIII securing the team title.

LIV chief executive Scott O'Neil told reporters on Wednesday he was optimistic about their reimagined plans for 2027, despite the loss of financial backing from Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (PIF), with players set to be equity owners and have their commercial rights restored.

  • LIV Golf chief 'optimistic' over league's future
  • Rory McIlroy warns of 'tough road back' for LIV golfers
  • What next for LIV Golf? Their story so far....
  • Get Sky Sports or stream golf with no contract

O'Neil confirmed an initial proposed calendar for five team championships and five individual tournaments, all scheduled around the majors, with DeChambeau heavily involved in discussions over their long-term future and appearing positive about how it could look.

"I think there's a lot of potential moving forward," DeChambeau said after his final round. "It has been an interesting ride, that's for sure. You know everything that we've gone through and the tough moments that we've had, but it's made us stronger.

"As much as we're transitioning from LIV 1.0 to 2.0, I have great thoughts about what could happen next year. I wish I could be more up front about it.

"Ultimately, I'm proud of the fact of what we've done - the good and some of the bad that we've unfortunately had, things that have occurred. I'm going to be real with it; not everything was perfect, but for the most part we've done a solid job.

"If there's one thing that I could say, it's we did something different in the game of golf, and I'm proud of that."

He later added as he walked away from his post-round TV interview: "I think there's something fun coming."

LIV has spent more than $5 billion in five years, pulling some of the world's best and upcoming talent away from traditional golf tours, with significant investment required for them to continue beyond this season.

O'Neil said he has a "good level of confidence" that a "critical mass of the right players" will return, with Rahm under contract next season but DeChambeau's set to expire at the end of this season.

Rahm finished the LIV Golf campaign with his third straight season points title and his second team crown in a row, with the Spaniard among those waiting to see what happens to the circuit.

"I'm looking forward to going home and helping my very pregnant wife with the kids," Rahm said. "The fourth one is due in October, and I'm happy to be dad for a few days before I get back to grinding for the Irish Open, and mainly looking forward to a haircut because I need one badly."

When asked whether LIV Golf's uncertain future made it hard to focus on the golf, Rahm added: "Not really. There's been a lot that's surrounded all of us for pretty much since we joined.

"At the end of the day, once we step on the golf course, it's just golf. Everything else goes away, and we just compete. It hasn't been any harder or easier than it was."

articles.title: PGA Tour: Rory McIlroy maintains concerns over game heading into Tour Championship despite late BMW Championship title push
articles.summary: Rory McIlroy finished third at the BMW Championship, four strokes behind winner Wyndham Clark; McIlroy overturned a five-shot deficit on the final day before falling short over the closing holes; McIlroy is back in action at the Tour Championship, live on Sky Sports from Thursday
articles.body:
Rory McIlroy admitted he is still not happy with his swing heading into the season-ending Tour Championship, despite narrowly missing out on victory at the BMW Championship.

McIlroy described his game as "so far away" from where it needed to be after a forgettable week at the FedEx St Jude Championship, where he ended 66th in a 68-man field, only to produce a much-improved performance in St Louis.

The world No 2 birdied three of the last four holes of his third round at Bellerive Country Club to get within five strokes of leader Wyndham Clark, setting up a Sunday pairing with the US Open champion, before pulling level with the American on the final day.

  • BMW Championship recap: Final round as it happened
  • Final BMW Championship leaderboard and other scores
  • Latest PGA Tour news, reports and highlights
  • Get Sky Sports or stream golf with no contract

McIlroy remained tied for the lead with three holes to play but eventually ended in third spot, four strokes back, as Clark produced a three-birdie finish to claim a three-shot victory and third PGA Tour win of the season.

"I'm closer [with his game] than I was at the start of the week," McIlroy admitted. "I'm still not in a spot where I'm super happy with where my game is or where my swing is, so I just have to keep working on it.

"It's nice to know, even when I'm not super happy with everything, I can still piece it together and get it around and still give myself a chance to win tournaments."

McIlroy capitalised on a two-shot swing at the first hole and recovered from bogeys at the fourth and seventh to post three birdies in a four-hole stretch from the eighth, pulling him level after Clark played his first 10 holes in three over.

Clark edged ahead with a 15-foot birdie at the 16th and found his own two-shot swing at the par-five next, making birdie as McIlroy dropped a shot, before finding another at the last to extend his winning margin over Patrick Cantlay.

"I felt like most of my game held up today," McIlroy added. "Obviously, going out in the final group and you're working on some stuff, you're just hoping that everything stays the way it is.

"I hit it well on the back nine. I gave myself plenty of chances. I just couldn't get a putt to drop there in those final few holes. I always felt like I needed to just get my nose ahead to really try to put the pressure on Wyndham [Clark] and I couldn't.

"We were tied there for a few holes and then when he made that putt on 16 for a two and I couldn't answer - that was obviously a huge moment in the round and in the tournament. Overall, encouraged with how I played this week and certainly something to build on going into East Lake."

Both players found the rough off the tee at the par-five 17th, where Clark elected to lay up on his way to a birdie as McIlroy went from bunker to bunker and carded a tournament-ending bogey.

"I tried to get it up a bit too far," McIlroy conceded. "I should have been taking that left bunker out of play. If you're going to lay it up, lay it up, so just another stupid decision with a lay-up on a par-five that cost me."

On whether he felt like he deserved the win, McIlroy explained to CBS Sports: "I can't be too disappointed. I'm probably not playing well enough to be disappointed that I didn't win.

"I had my chances on the back nine and hit a lot of good putts that didn't go in. Wyndham Clark stepped up when he needed too. His birdie on 16 was huge and the way he played the last three holes, he showed a lot of character."

articles.body:
Miyu Yamashita equaled the LPGA Tour's 72-hole scoring record in claiming a dominant, nine-stroke victory in the CPKC Women's Open..

The Japanese star's closing birdie on Sunday signed off a four-under final round of 66 to take her total for the week to 23 under par and 257 strokes, securing a wire-to-wire win in Edmonton.

Sei Young Kim also shot 257 in the 2018 Thornberry Creek LPGA Classic in Wisconsin, finishing 31 under.

A stroke ahead after Thursday's opening round, thanks to a course-record 62, Yamashita posted a 64 on Friday to open a five-shot lead, before carding a 65 on Saturday.

That had her six strokes ahead entering the final round at Royal Mayfair, Yamashita pushed her winning margin to nine for a tournament record in the Canadian national championship, breaking Jin Young Ko's 262 set in 2019 at Magna in Aurora, Ontario.

Yamashita's four LPGA Tour titles have come in four different countries. She won the Meijer LPGA Classic in the USA in June, after claiming a first major success at the AIG Women's Open title in Wales along with taking the Maybank Championship title in Malaysia last year. She has 13 Japan LPGA victories.

Fellow Japanese player Yuri Yoshida was second at 14 under after a closing 69. Kim was a further shot back after her final-round 67.

Seventeen-year-old Anna Huang was the top Canadian, signing off her week with an impressive 65 to tie for fourth at 12 under.

articles.title: 'Darth Vader Had More Fun,' Wyndham Clark Reacts to BMW Win After Pairing with McIlroy, Scheffler
articles.summary: For the second time this year, Wyndham Clark knew he wasn't the sentimental favorite as he went on to claim victory.
articles.body:
For the second time this year, Wyndham Clark knew he wasn't the sentimental favorite as he went on to claim victory.

Playing with Scottie Scheffler for the final round, Clark received a frosty reception from the crowd as he won the U.S. Open in June. Sunday was a case of déjà vu as he claimed the BMW Championship knowing full well the St. Louis fans were pulling for Rory McIlroy.

"Darth Vader had more fun," he said, per the Associated Press' Doug Ferguson . "... I know everyone maybe gives me a hard time and roots for other people. But I feel like I've kind of come into my own. Three wins in one season is my best year yet — coming off my worst year ever. I'm just really pleased where I'm at right now."

Bryson's lates post raises more LIV questions

Much like the U.S. Open, Clark didn't seal the deal in emphatic fashion. His even-par 70 on Sunday was his worst round of the tournament. Birdies on his last three holes kept him three shots clear of runner-up Patrick Cantlay.

This is already the biggest year of Clark's career. His three wins match how many he had entering the season.

The 32-year-old can potentially put quite the capper on 2026. The Tour Championship tees off Thursday at East Lake Golf Club in Atlanta, and the winner will pocket a $10 million prize.

articles.title: Trump planning visit to Ireland for tournament at his golf course
articles.summary: President Trump plans to head to Ireland next month to attend the Irish Open at his golf course in Doonbeg. articles.body:
President Trump plans to head to Ireland next month to attend the Irish Open at his golf course in Doonbeg.

Trump will be in Ireland on Sept. 12 and 13, the final two days of the tournament, a White House official told The Hill. The New York Post was first to report on the president’s upcoming trip.

Before attending the tournament, the president will join an event with U.S. Embassy workers and business officials, according to the White House official.

He will then attend the Irish Open, which will take place at Trump International Golf Links Ireland, located in County Clare on Ireland’s Atlantic coast. Trump purchased the property in 2014, before mounting his initial bid for president.

The president said in March he was going to “try” to attend the tournament.

“It would be an honor, but it was a great honor to be chosen. They only chose the best courses in the world for the … big opens. That’s one of the big ones, the Irish Open,” Trump said alongside Irish Taoiseach Micheál Martin in the Oval Office.

Two-time defending Masters champion Rory McIlroy will defend his Irish Open title at the tournament, set for Sept. 10-13.

McIlroy attended a state dinner honoring King Charles III at the White House in May, during which Trump saluted the golfer’s second consecutive Masters victory .

The president, an avid golfer, has attended multiple golf tournaments during his second term — including those at courses his company owns.

In May, he attended the final round of the PGA Tour’s Cadillac Championship at his Doral, Fla., resort. The LIV Golf league , meanwhile, held two of its 12 events this year at Trump-owned courses.

Trump also attended the second day of last September’s Ryder Cup at Bethpage Black Course in Farmingdale, N.Y.

While in office, the president has profited from the golf courses he owns. In 2025, seven of his clubs — five in the U.S. and two in Scotland — reported more than $252.5 million in revenue combined, according to Trump’s latest financial disclosure .

articles.title: Rep. Al Green files articles of impeachment against Trump again
articles.summary: Rep. Al Green (D-Texas) introduced articles of impeachment against President Trump on Monday, reviving his push to remove the president from office as Democrats debate how aggressively to confront Trump ahead of the 2026 midterm elections. Green’s resolution is aimed at impeaching Trump for high crimes and misdemeanors “committed in violation of the president’s mandated…
articles.body:
Rep. Al Green (D-Texas) introduced articles of impeachment against President Trump on Monday, reviving his push to remove the president from office as Democrats debate how aggressively to confront Trump ahead of the 2026 midterm elections.

Green’s resolution is aimed at impeaching Trump for high crimes and misdemeanors “committed in violation of the president’s mandated oath of office to preserve, protect, and defend the United States Constitution.” It accuses Trump of operating U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and Customs and Border Protection (CBP) “as his vicious, quota-driven, unaccountable paramilitary police forces.”

Democrats have urged the White House to reform its immigration enforcement tactics after the deaths of U.S. citizens and immigrants by ICE and Border Patrol officials. Among the most prominent cases was the death of Renee Good, a 37-year-old U.S. citizen and Minneapolis resident, who was shot by an immigration officer in January.

Weeks later, Border Patrol agents shot and killed Alex Pretti, a 37-year-old U.S. citizen and intensive care nurse, in Minneapolis. More recently, an ICE officer fatally shot Lorenzo Salgado Araujo, a Mexican immigrant, in Houston.

“President Trump has used ICE and CBP to suppress the First Amendment rights to free speech and a free press; violate the Fourth Amendment right to privacy and protections against unlawful searches and excessive force; and defy the Fifth and Fourteenth Amendment guarantees of due process and equal protection by allowing and encouraging racially targeted 7 arrests, unjustified detentions, and unjustified killings,” the resolution notes.

Green has previously introduced articles of impeachment against Trump, but his efforts have failed to garner the support needed to advance in the House. Green, for instance, filed an article of impeachment against Trump in June 2025, accusing the president of failing to notify or seek authorization from Congress before the U.S. launched strikes on three Iranian nuclear sites that summer.

The Texas lawmaker forced a vote on the article of impeachment. The measure was scuttled in a lopsided vote, 344-79, which saw most Democrats — including all the top Democratic leaders — siding with Republicans to put it to bed.

And in the first year of Trump’s first term, Green was the first Democrat to force impeachment articles to the floor — long before Democratic leaders were on board — accusing Trump of stirring racial tensions in the wake of the 2017 march of white supremacists in Charlottesville, Va.

Green lost the Democratic primary runoff for Texas’s 18th Congressional District to Rep. Christian Menefee (D-Texas) in May.

articles.title: Solheim Cup 2026: Angela Stanford names Megan Khang, Rose Zhang and Lindy Duncan as captain's picks, as Team USA squad confirmed
articles.summary: Team USA’s captain Angela Stanford has finalised her 12-player squad for September's Solheim Cup; captain's pick Lindy Duncan is one of two debutants in the side alongside Auston Kim; watch the Solheim Cup live from September 11-13 on Sky Sports Golf
articles.body:
Megan Khang, Rose Zhang and Lindy Duncan have been named as Angela Stanford's three captains' picks for next month's Solheim Cup, as Team USA's full 12-player squad was officially finalised on Monday.

Following this weekend's CPKC Women's Open, Andrea Lee and Alison Lee also both earned qualifying spots for Team USA via the Rolex Women's World Golf Rankings.

They will join Nelly Korda, Angel Yin, Jennifer Kupcho, Yealimi Noh, Auston Kim, Lauren Coughlin and Allisen Corpuz, who all qualified automatically for the tournament via the Solheim Cup points list.

  • Solheim Cup 2026: Teams, format and how qualifying worked
  • Who qualified for Team Europe and how did they do it?
  • Anna Nordqvist: Captaincy challenge 'more than expected'
  • Get Sky Sports or stream golf with no contract

Anna Nordqvist confirmed her four captain's picks earlier in August, with both sides now set to face off at Bernardus Golf in The Netherlands on September 11, and all three tournament days will be shown live on Sky Sports Golf.

Duncan, 35, and Kim, 26, are the only two rookies in Stanford's squad for September's tournament. Duncan is also the second-oldest Solheim Cup debutant since Nancy Scranton, who made her first Solheim Cup appearance in 2000, aged 39.

"It's been so much fun," Stanford told The Golf Channel when asked what the process of making her selections was like.

"Of course, we had our tough times, and it's about getting down to the moment that we have to tell people they did not make it. But we expected that, and I absolutely love the 12 players we have.

"We are ready to get to the Netherlands and represent the Red, White & Blue."

Experienced Solheim Cup players Lilia Vu, who has struggled with her form this season, and Lexi Thompson, who is expecting her first baby early next year, have both also missed out.

Lucy Li and Jenny Bae had also been in the running to feature but also missed out, having both missed the cut at this weekend's CPKC Women's Open.

Stanford's captain's picks

Khang brings a ton of experience to Team USA, with the 28-year-old having played in four Solheim Cups.

She played a pivotal role in helping Team USA defeat Team Europe at the Robert Trent Jones Golf Club in 2024, with Khang going undefeated, taking home a record of 3-0-0.

"When I got the call from Angela, I sat there for a little bit, and she was like: 'Are you going to smile?'" Khang said.

"I was shocked by it, and it's super cool to be picked. Once you play in one, you don't want to miss one and I can't wait to get to Bernardus Golf."

Zhang has featured in two Solheim Cups in 2023 and again in 2024, and, similar to Khang, she took home a perfect record of 4-0-0 in the 2024 event.

The 23-year-old has enjoyed a fine season on the LPGA Tour, making three top-10 finishes in 14 starts, and placed tied-eighth at The Standard Portland Classic last week.

"It was easy for me to include Rose," Stanford said. "Rose, she's been successful on different levels, and at each one, she's been a winner."

Duncan has enjoyed an excellent two years on the LPGA Tour, secured 14 top-25 finishes, notably placing tied-second at the 2025 Chevron Championship.

"It's pretty amazing to think about some of the times I've been through a couple of years ago," Duncan said. "I wouldn't have believed it if you had told me. I felt pretty close to stepping away from the game for a while.

"To have persevered through some tough times and have played well to make this team, it's truly an honour.

"It was always a dream and felt really far away for a long time. To have made it feels really incredible."

Who else features for Team USA?

Andrea Lee, who is set to feature in her third Solheim Cup, booked her place as the highest-ranked American player in the Rolex Women's World Golf Rankings not to qualify for the tournament via Team USA's Solheim Cup points list.

She has represented Team USA twice, booking her spot as an automatic qualifier on both occasions, and boasts a 3-2-2 record, notably pairing with Zhang in 2024 to claim two impressive foursome victories.

Alison Lee will also play in her third Solheim Cup, having enjoyed wins with Team USA at the 2015 and 2024 events.

The 31-year-old holds a record of 2-5-0 across seven matches and returns to compete at this year's event after becoming a mum last year.

She has enjoyed an excellent season on the LPGA Tour, which has included three top-five finishes, placing tied-third at both the Mizuho Americas Open and Dow Championship.

Meanwhile, world No 1 Korda tops the list of names who have qualified via the Solheim Cup points list, with the American having won four times this season, including her victory at The Chevron Championship in April and her US Open triumph in June.

"I'm really proud of Nelly because she has really grown into this," Stanford said.

"Just her demeanour and her calmness. She carries the weight of our tour quite a bit. She has grown into that, and I'm very proud of her."

Yin and Kupcho also return to Team USA, and both will play in their fourth Solheim Cups.

Noh, who finished third at the AIG Women's Open, ranked fourth on Team USA's Solheim Cup points list, while Kim will make her debut at the event.

Coughlin and Corpuz make up the final two players who qualified for Team USA automatically.

articles.title: Bryson DeChambeau Makes Cryptic IG Post amid Questions of LIV Golf Future
articles.summary: Bryson DeChambeau may have bid his farewell to LIV Golf on Monday amid questions about the future of the organization.
articles.body:
Bryson DeChambeau may have bid his farewell to LIV Golf on Monday amid questions about the future of the organization.

The star posed a cryptic post on Instagram featuring several photos from LIV Golf, along with the caption "It was a good run."

The post on Monday comes after optimistic comments from DeChambeau last week. He said Thursday that he hopes people are "open-minded" about the league's future and wants it to receive "one more shot."

"It's tough, it's not easy," DeChambeau said. "We definitely have a lot against us."

Speculation around LIV Golf's future began after Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund announced it would no longer finance the league after initially funding the tour and investing billions of dollars. Since it pulled out, LIV Golf has cancelled two events.

According to ESPN's Paolo Uggetti , the league "has also faced multiple lawsuits from vendors over missed payments and cut back on its offerings at events amid financial uncertainty."

DeChambeau also said last week that he hopes fans "can see that we actually bring value to the game of golf." That came after Rory McIlroy questioned whether they do.

"I mean, I would argue, have they brought value to LIV?" McIlroy told reporters. "I think the PGA Tour's in a really good spot."

LIV CEO Scott O'Neil announced that LIV Golf signed a term sheet with a new investor, and he's also working toward a new version of the league that would give players smaller purses and equity.

But O'Neil's efforts may not be enough to keep DeChambeau or other stars around. Brooks Koepka already left LIV earlier this year, and James Corrigan of The Telegraph reported last week that sources "are almost resigned" to Jon Rahm leaving.

Rahm and DeChambeau exiting in quick succession would only make it more difficult for LIV to gather funding.

When Koepka returned to the PGA Tour, it came with financial penalties, including a forfeiture of player equity and a $5 million charity contribution. Should Rahm and DeChambeau return to the tour, they would presumably face similar stipulations.

articles.title: Ian Poulter undecided about his future with LIV Golf but hopes the league can continue, amid financial concerns
articles.summary: Ian Poulter was one of the first players to join LIV Golf back in 2022 but the five-time Ryder Cup winner says he is undecided on whether he will continue to play on the circuit into the future
articles.body:
Ian Poulter hasn't made up his mind on whether he will continue to play on LIV Golf next season, but hopes the league can continue to operate next year, amid concerns over its funding.

Alongside his Majesticks GC team-mate Lee Westwood, Poulter was among one of the first players to join the rebel league back in 2022.

But after LIV Golf concluded its 2026 season in Indianapolis last weekend, Poulter took to Instagram to explain he was undecided if he would play on the tour into next year, adding that he was 'proud' of what LIV has achieved.

  • DeChambeau: There's 'something fun coming'
  • Rory McIlroy warns of 'tough road back' for LIV golfers
  • What next for LIV Golf? Their story so far....
  • Get Sky Sports or stream golf with no contract

"This final phase has been tough and none of us knows exactly what comes next," the five-time Ryder Cup winner said. "My thoughts are especially with the businesses and suppliers still owed money. Some are small businesses and I sincerely hope those situations are dealt with properly and quickly.

"It would be a real shame if LIV 2.0 doesn't happen. There are players who would love a strong global platform to play on and countries and fans who want us back.

"Some players will stay, some may go. As for me, I may stay or take some time off. I genuinely haven't decided yet.

"I know some people didn't agree with my decision to join LIV. I've never hidden from the financial side.

"Golfers have received appearance fees around the world throughout my career and still do today. LIV gave me a significant opportunity late in my career and I took it.

"People make career decisions every day based on opportunity, family and financial security. Professional sport is no different."

After paying off their fines for playing in the rebel league, Poulter and Lee Westwood will return to play on the DP World Tour in October and for the Alfred Dunhill Links Championship.

It comes as speculation is continuing to mount over LIV Golf's future and the futures of many of the players currently playing on the tour.

LIV Golf CEO Scott O'Neil announced earlier this month that it had found a new 'unnamed' lead investor, after Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (PIF) revealed it would be cutting its funding to LIV Golf at the conclusion of the 2026 season, leaving LIV bosses looking for new investors.

A term sheet has been signed for the commercial arrangement, with O'Neil explaining that he was hopeful the league would enter into a transaction with its new investor in September.

LIV Golf's Team Championship event in Michigan, which was scheduled to be played this weekend, was subsequently cancelled, raising more alarm bells over the league's future.

Meanwhile, Bryson DeChambeau insisted "something fun was coming" and there was "a lot of potential" in LIV Golf to continue into next year.

Poulter, a three-time winner on the PGA Tour and a 12-time winner on the DP World Tour, has not won an individual or team title with LIV Golf in his five years on the circuit.

"It hasn't always been easy, and it was never going to be," Poulter said, reflecting on his time on the circuit. "Building something new and challenging the status quo was always going to bring challenges and criticism. I sincerely thank everyone who supported me, our team and LIV throughout the journey.

"We've taken this great game around the world to countries and cities that genuinely embraced us. Playing in front of crowds of over 100,000 fans at some events was truly special. To everyone who came out and supported us - thank you. You were class.

"A special thank you to my team-mates Lee [Westwood], Henrik [Stenson], Sam [Horsfield] and Laurie [Canter], every member of the LIV and Majesticks staff and, most importantly, the fans who supported me.

"At Majesticks GC we built an incredible team, but what I'm most proud of is Littlesticks. We've taken golf directly into the PE curriculum of over 200 schools and put clubs into the hands of more than 40,000 kids. That's a legacy our whole team should be incredibly proud of."

articles.title: Callaway, Good Good Golf apologize for ad in which a man shoves a woman to the ground over a driver
articles.summary: Callaway said it never should have approved the ad in the first place.
articles.body:
Callaway and Good Good Golf are scrambling to apologize after a joint ad backfired in a major way. The now-deleted ad — which featured a man shoving a woman to the ground over a driver — drew intense criticism for making light of domestic violence.

Good Good Golf originally posted the video Friday. A day later, however, the video was deleted and the company released a statement apologizing for it.

Our statement on the recent driver ad that we decided to remove: pic.twitter.com/oFxO3eFZV1 — Good Good Golf (@goodgood_golf) August 22, 2026

Our statement on the recent driver ad that we decided to remove: pic.twitter.com/oFxO3eFZV1

The ad was for a co-branded driver with Callaway. In it, Good Good Golf co-founder Garrett Clark runs over and shoves content creator Alexis Miestowski to the ground before she can touch Clark's driver. Clark then sinisterly utters, "Do not touch my new driver" as Miestowski lays on the ground.

Here's the now-deleted ad in case that description doesn't sound worrisome enough:

Good Good Golf has deleted and apologized for this video where a man shoves a woman to the ground for reaching for his new Callaway club. Social media users, including several high-profile golf personalities, described the ad as scary and endorsing violence against women. — Front Office Sports (@FOS) August 23, 2026

Good Good Golf has deleted and apologized for this video where a man shoves a woman to the ground for reaching for his new Callaway club. Social media users, including several high-profile golf personalities, described the ad as scary and endorsing violence against women.

Early Tuesday, Callaway responded, putting out a lengthy statement apologizing for the video being approved and released.

In the statement, Callaway clarified that the video was produced by Good Good Golf, but was approved by Callaway before it was posted. "That approval should never have happened," the post stated.

Callaway clarified it is "unequivocally against discrimination, domestic violence, or threatening behavior of any kind." The company also announced it was launching internal and external investigations and said it has already changed its approval process to ensure "this will never happen again."

Good Good started as a YouTube channel, but eventually grew into a golf sponsor. The company is the title sponsor of the Good Good Golf Championship, which will take place in November.

articles.title: The Match-Play TOUR Championship Is (Finally) Coming. Here's How It'll Work.
articles.summary: We've never been more back!
articles.body:
The TOUR Championship is going to look unrecognizable when the PGA TOUR implements the changes it has planned for 2028.

In two years, we'll see the top 90 players of the Championship Series advance to the "Championship Series Finale." This will be a 72-hole, stroke-play event that will not only finalize the season-long points race, but also determine the field for the 32-man new-look TOUR Championship.

The new TOUR Championship will be a two-week, match-play event contested at iconic venues the TOUR doesn't often see (or never has). According to the Sports Business Journal , the list of potential venues includes Sleepy Hollow, Los Angeles Country Club, and Interlachen.

The first week will be the group stage, where the field will be split into eight groups of four players. Each player will face the other three players in his group, and the top two seeds from each group will move on to the next week.

The final week will feature the 16 players playing four rounds of match play. It won't look like March Madness, where if you lose, you go home, all 16 players will participate in all four rounds. The final two undefeated players will battle for the title of TOUR Champion.

Confused? Well, this video from the TOUR makes it easy to understand.

TOUR CEO Brian Rolapp wrote this in a statement sent out on Tuesday:

"From the beginning, the goal of the Future Competition Committee was to create an easier-to-follow competitive model for our fans with greater consequence and a stronger season-long narrative. Throughout this process, we listened carefully to our fans, players and partners. One message came through clearly: the culmination of our season should be worthy of the journey it takes to get there. The result is a season-ending structure that rewards excellence over the course of the year while building toward a reimagined TOUR Championship. We are creating something different, something distinct within professional golf that can resonate far beyond it."

articles.title: PGA Tour Announces New Playoff Format, Match-Play Bracket for 2028 Season
articles.summary: The PGA Tour is adopting a new playoff format that will start in 2028.
articles.body:
The PGA Tour is adopting a new playoff format that will start in 2028.

Per a release from the PGA Tour, the format will feature three components starting with the PGA TOUR Championship Series Finale followed by a two-week TOUR Championship.

The top 90 players on the championship series points list will qualify for the PGA TOUR Championship Series Finale, which will be a traditional 72-hole stroke-play event to crown a tournament champion and No. 1 finisher on the overall points list.

The first week of the TOUR Championship will feature 32 players split into eight groups of four competing in a three-day match play event. The top two players in each group will then advance to the second week in a four-day, head-to-head match-play bracket with players moving on based on their win-loss record.

The two players who remain undefeated after the first three days will square off on the final day to determine the TOUR champion.

"The conclusion of the season should be worthy of the journey it takes to get there," Tiger Woods said Tuesday. "Today's announcement is a result of the hard work and passion of our players. Excited to usher in a new era of match play on the PGA Tour."

The PGA Tour will unveil the dates and locations for the three events on Feb. 22, 2027. Eligibility for the Championship Series will be be announced following a Sept. 14 board meeting.

Tuesday's announcement comes in the wake of the Tour revealing earlier this summer that the 2028 season would feature a dramatic change to the entire PGA schedule with two separate series of tournaments.

The tournaments are the PGA Tour Championship Series and PGA Tour Challenger Series, with 15 events expected to comprise the Championship Series. All of those events will have a prize purse of at least $20 million.

The Challenger Series will feature emerging talent competing with players looking to return to the top level with a minimum of 20 events comprising the series, which will run concurrently with the Championship Series. Prize purses for the Challenger Series will be a minimum of $4 million.

This new playoff structure will replace the current FedEx Cup playoff that features a progressive elimination structure over three tournaments, all of which utilize the traditional 72-hole stroke-play format.

The FedEx Cup playoff consists of the St. Jude Championship, BMW Championship and TOUR Championship. The top 70 players make the initial field with 20 being eliminated after each of the first two events.

This year's FedEx Cup playoff will conclude this weekend with the TOUR Championship at East Lake Golf Club in Atlanta, Georgia. Wyndham Clark won the BMW Championship last weekend with a score of 17-under par.

articles.title: Nick Faldo: LIV returnees should 'eat humble pie' before rejoining DP World Tour
articles.summary: Sir Nick Faldo says LIV golfers seeking a return to the DP World Tour may have to "eat a bit of humble pie" before regaining eligibility for the European-based circuit.
articles.body:
Sir Nick Faldo says LIV golfers seeking a return to the DP World Tour may have to "eat a bit of humble pie" before regaining eligibility for the European-based circuit.

LIV's 2026 season ended last Sunday in Indianapolis after this week's cancellation of the breakaway tour's Team Championship in Michigan.

Tyrrell Hatton, Tom McKibbin and Adrian Meronk are competing instead at the Husqvarna British Masters starting on Thursday.

Six-time major champion Faldo is promoting the Belfry tournament while LIV's boss Scott O'Neil continues his quest to replace Saudi Arabian funding. He wants $350m (Â£258m) investment to keep the league operating next year.

"I'm hearing there are more players wanting to leave LIV than want to stay," Faldo told BBC Sport.

"So it doesn't sound good for them for the future."

Hatton, McKibbin and Meronk are able to compete as DP World Tour members after accepting a deal that allowed them to play both tours without sanction this year.

For his walk on music at the Indianapolis tournament last week, Hatton chose Queen's I Want to Break Free, interpreted as a firm signal that the Englishman wants to leave the tour that began in 2022.

Hatton has recent tournament wins that protect his DP World status. Two-time major champion Jon Rahm also has exemptions that would qualify him for the tour should he quit the previously Saudi Arabia-funded outfit.

But Faldo is clear that it should not be overly easy for LIV players to walk straight back onto the DP World Tour.

"How do they actually give them a route back?" Faldo added.

"You know, given the way they've disrupted - go and start again. Go back to tour school.

"Hey, you might have to eat a bit of humble pie and say, well, I want to be a proper golfer again, and so I've got to start back where I'm meant to be and I'll work my way up the good old way with my skills and my scoring."

DeChambeau proud of what LIV has achieved Published 1 day ago

DeChambeau proud of what LIV has achieved

Discussions begin on how to reintegrate returnees

How potential returnees are to be treated was high on the agenda when the DP World Tour's tournament committee met on Tuesday afternoon.

PGA chief executive officer Brian Rolapp said there are no "current plans" to offer LIV players a route back.

"I don't know the future of LIV," he added.

"We've been consistent. Anyone who's interested in coming to the PGA Tour needs to demonstrate that they are relieved of their contractual commitments or any tail obligations they might have in that legacy model."

While America's PGA Tour imposed blanket one-year bans on members who competed on the LIV tour, their European counterparts take a more nuanced approach.

With many leading Europeans based in the United States, the Wentworth-based organisation would like as many big names as it can get.

At the same time they have to protect the rest of the membership who remained loyal to the tour.

"It is a difficult jigsaw to piece together and we have to work out how to treat these players should they want to leave LIV and rejoin," said a senior tour source.

Faldo said: "We can negotiate. If a player has some form of exemption on the tour already, someone like Rahm would obviously carry it through majors and that sort of thing.

"But all the other guys, you know, they did cause quite a disruption in the world of golf. You know, they were in a way invited into LIV. And that's not how golf is, is it?

"We all had to do the good old Monday qualifying back in the day, 50 blooming years ago. I personally think that's the way it should be, you start again and climb the ladder."

Chile's Joaquin Niemann was one of the most successful players on the LIV tour, amassing more than Â£60m in prize money. But the 27-year-old is currently ineligible for both the PGA and DP World Tours.

Lee Westwood, Ian Poulter and Sergio Garcia - all distinguished Ryder Cup players for Europe - are others whose status could be up for debate.

Exciting young Spaniard Josele Ballester and American Peter Uihlein are LIV golfers who have entered the first stage of DP World Tour qualifying school at Huddersfield on 2 September.

articles.title: PGA Tour: Tour Championship to be played in a matchplay format from 2028 amid huge shake-up to season-ending schedule
articles.summary: From 2028, the PGA Tour's Tour Championship will be played in a matchplay format, with Rory McIlroy among those to welcome the switch, calling it "a big swing";Watch this week's Tour Championship live on Sky Sports Golf from Thursday
articles.body:
The PGA Tour has announced that the Tour Championship will be played in a two-week matchplay format as part of a new season-ending structure which will be implemented from the 2028 season, with Rory McIlroy among those to welcome the move.

PGA Tour chief executive Brian Rolapp announced the plans on Tuesday ahead of this week's Tour Championship at East Lake in Atlanta.

"It's certainly different. But it's cool. I think they've taken a big swing, and conceptually, I think I really like it," McIlroy said at his pre-torunament press conference.

  • How will promotion and relegation work in 2028 season?
  • Latest PGA Tour news, reports and highlights
  • Get Sky Sports or stream golf with no contract

From 2028 onwards, the current series of FedExCup Playoffs, which are played in a stroke play format, will be replaced by:

  • A 72-hole stroke play PGA Tour Championship Series Finale featuring the top 90 golfers on the PGA Tour season-long points list
  • The top 32 players on the PGA Tour's points list at the end of the PGA Tour Championship Series Finale will qualify for the Tour Championship, a standalone two-week match play event
  • The match play tournament will be similar to the World Cup, with groups and knockouts

It will be the first time in the PGA Tour's history that the Tour Championship has been decided over a match play format, and is also the first time that the format has been played on the tour since the 2023 WGC Dell Technologies Match Play.

It is one of a series of major schedule shake-ups coming to the PGA Tour, with the US circuit also set to introduce a new two-tier system which will feature promotion and relegation.

"Throughout this process, we listened carefully to our fans, players and partners," Rolapp said.

"One message came through clearly: the culmination of our season should be worthy of the journey it takes to get there.

"The result is a season-ending structure that rewards excellence over the course of the year while building toward a reimagined Tour Championship. We are creating something different, something distinct within professional golf that can resonate far beyond it."

McIlroy added: "I think all the incentives are there, and the regular season champion is going to be adequately rewarded after that final stroke-play event, and then the Tour Championship match play is going to be completely different.

"It's sort of a departure from what we've had the last few years, but I do think it'll be a great thing."

How will the new PGA Tour postseason work?

Throughout the 2028 season, players will compete to win points as normal throughout regular-season tour events, in a similar fashion to the current FedExCup system.

The season-long points race will then conclude at the new PGA Tour Championship Series Finale, a 72-hole stroke play event.

The top 90 players in the year-long points race rankings will compete at the event, which will confirm the season-ending points race leader and final rankings for the year.

After the PGA Tour Championship Series Finale, the top 32 players in the year-end points rankings will then gain a place at the Tour Championship.

How will the new Tour Championship work?

The revamped Tour Championship will take place the week after the PGA Tour Championship Series Finale, with a field of 32 players competing over a three-round group stage, akin to the FIFA World Cup.

Players will be seeded, depending on their standing in the final season-long points race list.

Each golfer will square off against the other players from their group, with the top two players in each group advancing to week two of the Tour Championship.

Should a tie take place following the end of the group stage, a play-off will occur.

Sixteen players will then advance to week two of the match play final, where the Tour Champion will be confirmed.

Players will then compete in a four-round match play competition. The final two undefeated players will duke it out for the title.

A player's record and final standings at the Tour Championship will be determined by their record throughout the two-week match play event.

"Each week of the Tour Championship will be played at a different course," Rolapp added.

"This new format creates an exciting opportunity to showcase some of the most renowned venues in our sport, including places the modern tour has never been before."

Venues for the 2028 PGA Tour Championship Series Finale and Tour Championship will be confirmed in February 2027, with the US circuit explaining it will rotate hosting duties among "prestigious courses" and some venues the tour has not been able to feature in the past.

Woods backs new PGA Tour postseason structure

Writing on X on Tuesday, Tiger Woods expressed his excitement at the proposed changes.

"The conclusion of the season should be worthy of the journey it takes to get there," Woods said.​

"Today's announcement is a result of the hard work and passion ​of our players.

"Excited to usher in a new era of match play on the PGA Tour".

Faldo: I am delighted by this news

Sir Nick Faldo told The Sky Sports Golf Podcast:

"Everyone is asking how you can get some excitement back into the game of golf.

"A lot of people might disagree, but it's match play!

"You can pick the characters against each other rather than golf being almost like a wall.

"You can then get a bit of spice going on. We might get some great historic matches going on instead of seeing guys going nuts shooting 10 or 12 under.

"I'm delighted they're bringing more match play back.

"When I used to do TV, we said the second-best day, after The Masters, was the first day of the WGC Dell Technologies Match Play.

"Back before they changed it to a round robin, 64 players started, 34 went home, and nobody wants to go home!

"That was the best excitement for a day's golf!"

articles.title: Solheim Cup: Chance to regain trophy offers 'extra incentive' says wildcard Leona Maguire
articles.summary: Ireland's Leona Maguire says the opportunity for Europe to reclaim the Solheim Cup from the United States offers added incentive before the contest in the Netherlands in September.
articles.body:
Ireland's Leona Maguire says the opportunity to regain the Solheim Cup offers an "extra incentive" for Team Europe as they prepare to face the United States at Bernardus Golf in the Netherlands next month.

Maguire was part of the team which contested the 2024 edition as the US ran out 15.5-12.5 winners in Virginia.

The 31-year-old also participated in Europe's victory on Ohio in 2021 and the drawn encounter in Andalusia, which saw the Europeans retain the trophy.

Captain Anna Nordqvist chose Maguire as one of two wildcard picks for this year's event in Cromvoirt from 11-13 September.

Maguire will compete in the Women's Irish Open at the K Club in County Kildare this week, her last competitive action before the team contest in the Netherlands.

"Hopefully have a great week here [at the Irish Open] and then a week off to recharge and go again for the Solheim," Maguire told BBC Sport.

"Solheim's a special event every two years and a home Solheim is even more special.

"We've got a young team this year, an exciting team and looking forward to getting over to the Netherlands for that."

'Once you're part of one, you don't want to miss any more'

The 31-year-old became the first Irish player to represent Europe in the competition when she was selected for the 2021 version and broke the all-time rookie points record for either the Solheim Cup or Ryder Cup with a contribution of 4.5 points as the away team triumphed 15-13.

The County Cavan woman's overall individual record in the competition after also taking part in the two subsequent editions reads eight wins, one half and three defeats.

"It's one of my favourite events. It's a team event which we don't get to do very often and matchplay which I love," she explained.

"I think once you're part of one Solheim, the same as the Ryder Cup, you don't want to miss any more.

"It's competitive, there's no money on the line, it's all just for pride and all the rest. You're doing whatever you can to help your teammates and the team.

"We obviously lost the last one so there's an extra incentive to try and bring it back this time."

Maguire, a two-time winner on the LPGA Tour and a one-time victor on the Ladies European Tour, hopes the backing of home supporters can help Europe reclaim the trophy at the 20th running of the event.

"Home support always helps as well. There was massive Irish support in Spain two times ago so hopefully a few Irish will maybe make the trip to Holland."

articles.title: PGA Tour Commissioner Currently Has No Plans to Offer LIV Golfers 'Returning Member Program'
articles.summary: Despite the uncertainty about LIV Golf's future, the PGA Tour is not planning to offer players who left to join the upstart circuit a path back.
articles.body:
Despite the uncertainty about LIV Golf's future, the PGA Tour is not planning to offer players who left to join the upstart circuit a path back.

Speaking to reporters on Tuesday, PGA Tour commissioner Brian Rolapp explained the Returning Member Program isn't being considered at this point that would allow LIV golfers an opportunity to back on the Tour.

"No, currently there's no current plans for [the] Returning Member Program like you saw earlier this year," Rolapp said.

Bryson's lates post raises more LIV questions

The PGA Tour adopted the Returning Member Program in January, citing fan research that showed a "clear desire" to see the best players competing more often and "timely inquiries" from non-PGA Tour players who had an interest in returning.

Under the rules of the program, players were eligible who participated in "unauthorized tournaments", have not been part on the PGA Tour for a minimum of two years and won at least one of THE PLAYERS, Masters, U.S. Open, PGA Championship and/or The Open Championship anytime between 2022 to '25.

Players had to apply for the program between Jan. 12-Feb. 2 and it only applied for the 2026 season, meaning they could not indicate now in order to return to the Tour in 2027.

The program requires participants to appear in at least 15 cosponsored and approved tournaments during the 2026 PGA Tour season. There were also financial penalties attached, including a $5 million donation to charity.

Brooks Koepka, Jon Rahm, Bryson DeChambeau and Cameron Smith were four players who left to join LIV Golf and were offered the chance to participate. Koepka was the only one who accepted the offer.

Per The Athletic's Gabby Herzig , Koepka's estimated financial penalties could end up between $51-85 million because he won't qualify for the player equity program until 2031 and doesn't receive any share of FedEx Cup bonus money this year in addition to the charitable donation.

LIV Golf's future has been unclear in the wake of the Saudi Arabia Public Investment Fund announcing it was pulling its funding. LIV CEO Scott O'Neil said in a statement released on Aug. 5 that the league has an "agreement in place" with a lead investor and they "anticipate finalizing terms in the coming weeks, with the goal of entering a transaction in September" to keep it going at least through 2027.

The 2026 LIV Golf season ended one week early with an event in Indianapolis over the weekend because the planned team championship event in Michigan that would have been played from Aug. 27-30 was canceled.

It marked the second canceled event on the schedule for LIV this year. New Orleans was set to host a tournament from June 25-28 that got was officially postponed due to what it said was an attempt to "avoid the peak summer heat" in the area.

LIV Golf was founded in 2021 and played its first season the following year. The league attempted to become an alternative to the PGA Tour and signed several top stars away with incredibly lucrative contracts.

Rahm was believed to be the highest-paid player on the circuit with a deal worth $300 million, followed by Phil Mickelson at $200 million and Koepka at $130 million. DeChambeau and Dustin Johnson both received $125 million.

articles.title: PGA Tour: Changes to play-off structure for 2028 a 'big swing' says Rory McIlroy
articles.summary: Back-to-back Masters champion Rory McIlroy believes the PGA Tour are giving fans what they want by changing their end-of-season play-offs to matchplay.
articles.body:
Back-to-back Masters champion Rory McIlroy believes the PGA Tour are giving fans what they want by introducing matchplay to their end-of-season play-offs.

PGA Tour CEO Brian Rolapp confirmed on Thursday that from 2028 the Tour Championship will be played across two weeks, at two different courses, and adopt a head-to-head format.

World number two McIlroy, who is a three-time winner of the FedEx Cup, feels the return of matchplay to the PGA Tour for the first time since 2023 shows fans have been listened to by the decision-makers.

"I think the PGA Tour and the Future Competition Committee and Brian and everyone involved have really taken on board what the fans have been calling for and have wanted, which is matchplay," said the Northern Irishman, 37.

"Brian took me through the plan last week for the first time. I didn't really know anything about it. It's certainly different.

"Two weeks, two different venues, but it's cool. I think they've taken a big swing, and conceptually, I think I really like it."

The FedEx Cup play-offs have have gone through numerous iterations across their two decades, presently consisting of a three-event strokeplay series which begins with the top 70 players from the season-long points list.

This week's concluding Tour Championship at East Lake in Atlanta will have a $40m (Â£29.3m) purse, and while the events have undoubtedly been lucrative for players, there have been consistent questions regarding fan engagement.

McIlroy added: "I think they've been great for players. Obviously we play for a ton of money, and it's sort of like the culmination of the entire season.

"The players have been rewarded. I think what the Tour are really trying to do is listen to the fans and what they want, and I think this idea of matchplay over two weeks is something that came mostly from what the people that watch golf wanted, so I think that's a really good thing."

The revised play-offs are only part of the changes coming to the PGA Tour in 2028 with a Championship and Challenger series to be established with promotion and relegation between the two.

With a regular season consisting of 15 events and a schedule which will run from February to August, McIlroy hoped more star players primarily based on the PGA Tour will follow his lead and play an increasing number of events on the DP World Tour.

The six-time major winner said: "I think if the PGA Tour are going to play from February through to August, DP World Tour have five months where, with the help of the PGA Tour and maybe some others, [it] can really shine a spotlight on international golf and put on some of the biggest international events in golf.

"I think with what the PGA Tour has been through with changing its competitive model and its structure, I think if the DP World Tour could do something similar, where you host all of your best events in that five-month time frame, it would allow guys to take up membership, to then have something to play for at the end of the DP World Tour season - if they choose to do that."

articles.title: Illinois WR Jayshon Platt likely out for start of season
articles.summary: The receiving room is getting thin.
articles.body:
As the Illini look to open the season, the team now faces some early challenges regarding injuries.

Highly touted FAU transfer Jayshon Platt will now likely miss the season opener against UAB, and potentially more.

Head coach Bret Bielema weighed in on Tuesday: "When the injury happened, we didn't know the exact timeline on it… Whether he's back week 1, week 3, or week 4, I don't really know at this point."

Platt, who came off a season where he captured 720 yards and 5 touchdowns, is viewed as one of the focal points of the Illini's offense going into this season. His talent is backed up with a recent nomination to the preseason Biletnikoff Award Watch List, which is given to the best receiver in the country.

The receiver room, under Justin Stepp, was already thinner than expected. After earlier news that FIU transfer Alex Perry will be sidelined potentially the entire season, even more weight was placed onto Platt and other receivers. Now that two critical transfer additions are sidelined, Illinois will have to look elsewhere for production.

Illinois was able to retain Collin Dixon and Hudson Clement , who will now be the headliners of this offense with the absence of Platt and Perry. I would expect these two to have a much heavier workload, especially early in the season.

Some younger, more inexperienced options may get the chance to flourish as well. Central Illinois native Brayden Trimble has been talked highly of in camp, so expect him to see the field early this season.

Illinois may also rely more than desired on the run game. With an experienced backfield full of playmakers, the coaching staff can trust this group to move the chains.

Losing another receiver is not the news fans or the coaching staff wanted to hear, especially 2 weeks before kickoff. However, Bielema has proven that he can adapt to sudden changes in playstyle and roster construction. With gameday just around the corner, it's going to be interesting to see how Illinois adjusts to these major changes.

articles.title: PGA chief says 'no current plans' for LIV stars to return
articles.summary: The PGA currently has no plans to offer LIV Golf stars like Bryson DeChambeau and Jon Rahm a pathway back from the struggling breakaway tour, chief executive...
articles.body:
The PGA currently has no plans to offer LIV Golf stars like Bryson DeChambeau and Jon Rahm a pathway back from the struggling breakaway tour, chief executive officer Brian Rolapp said Tuesday.

Launched in 2022, LIV caused shockwaves in the golf world as it spent billions of dollars luring top players away from the traditional PGA, but its survival is now deeply uncetain.

Having lost their Saudi investors, LIV organizers have promised a slimmed-down "2.0" version next year with new investors, but several key players have been linked with exits.

While the PGA Tour offered a temporary path back for some LIV players -- five-time major winner Brooks Koepka in January took advantage, paying financial penalties -- no repeats are planned, said Rolapp.

"Currently there's no current plans for Returning Member Program like you saw earlier this year," he said, ahead of this week's season-ending Tour Championship in Atlanta, Georgia.

The PGA has banned LIV players from its events, insisting any player wishing to return must first entirely cut ties with LIV, and Rolapp told Tuesday's press conference that "rules matter."

"Accountability and discipline are essential to any organization, and certainly for the integrity of the TOUR and for the game," he said.

Rolapp said it was impossible to speculate on if and how other LIV players could one day return to the PGA because "I don't know the future of LIV."

"We've been consistent. Anyone who's interested in coming to the PGA TOUR needs to demonstrate that they are relieved of their contractual commitments or any tail obligations they might have in that legacy model," he said.

"Brooks certainly did that, and until then, we weren't really able to consider anything seriously. I would say the same thing here."

LIV organizers have vowed to return next year with a slimmed-down schedule, smaller prizes and new investors.

Speaking at LIV's season-ending Indianapolis event Sunday, DeChambeau said he was "proud" of what the tour has achieved, and said he had "great thoughts about what could happen next year."

But on Monday he published an enigmatic post on Instagram -- photos of several LIV victories, with the caption "It was a good run."

articles.title: Golf giant Callaway apologizes after ad sparks outcry
articles.summary: Golf equipment giant Callaway issued an apology on Tuesday for a now-cancelled advert which showed a male golfer shoving a female player to the ground when s...
articles.body:
Golf equipment giant Callaway issued an apology on Tuesday for a now-cancelled advert which showed a male golfer shoving a female player to the ground when she reaches for his new driver.

The commercial, which was released online last week before being pulled, triggered a backlash over its depiction of violence against women, in addition to calls for a boycott of Callaway products.

Callaway golf chief executive Chip Brewer said in a statement on Tuesday that the company had launched an investigation into how the advert -- produced by golf media firm Good Good Golf -- had been approved.

"Last week Good Good Golf and Callaway posted a video to promote a co-branded driver," Brewer said in a statement.

"While the video was produced by Good Good, it was approved by Callaway prior to posting. That approval should never have happened. Mistakes were made and we are taking the matter very seriously.

"As we deal with the consequences of our mistake and complete our investigations, I want to make it clear that we sincerely apologize for the video.

"The content was inappropriate and does not reflect our values. To be clear: we are unequivocally against discrimination, domestic violence or threatening behavior of any kind... I assure you we will learn from this and do better."

The online advert showed Good Good co-founder Garrett Clark barging Epson Tour professional player Alexis Miestowski to the ground when she attempts to reach for his driver, before warning her: "Do not touch my new driver."

Good Good Golf, which centers its business around a successful YouTube channel aimed at bringing a younger audience to the sport, had already apologized for the controversial advert.

"We posted a video to our channels that ultimately depicted actions that are not aligned with our values as a brand," Good Good said in a statement.

"We have since taken that content down. And sincerely apologize. Good Good has always stood for making the game of golf more inclusive to all, and we will continue to ensure that is our mission moving forward."

Good Good's rise will see the company be the title sponsor for the PGA Tour's inaugural Good Good Championship in Austin, Texas in November.

PGA Tour chief executive Brian Rolapp said on Tuesday the circuit was dismayed by the advert and Good Good's handling of the controversy.

"I think what we saw was concerning, is clearly not aligned with PGA TOUR values. We take it very seriously," Rolapp said.

"I think their initial response was disappointing. It was a bit defensive and late.

"But I think the responses are getting better. I think we've seen some things this morning, we've had some conversations with them, so we'll continue to monitor and work with them going forward. But no, we were disappointed with what we saw."

articles.title: Seve Ballesteros Mastered Speed With One Clever Putting Trick
articles.summary: Discover the specific putting adjustment Seve Ballesteros used to control green speed and cut down three-putts, according to new reporting from Golf.com.
articles.body:
Seve Ballesteros changed how the game was played on the greens. His ability to read speed was legendary, but it wasn't magic. It was a specific trick he used to dial in his distance and reduce those costly three-putts. This method allowed the Spanish legend to navigate fast surfaces with a feel that others could not match. The story of his technique has resurfaced in recent coverage, shedding light on a skill that defined his career.

According to Golf.com, Seve Ballesteros used this clever trick on the greens to dial in his speed. Melton notes that Ballesteros focused intensely on reducing three-putts through this specific adjustment. The article places the story in the "Latest In Instruction" section, indicating its value for modern players looking to improve. Melton, the associate game-improvement editor for GOLF.com, has deep roots in the sport, having worked with the Texas Golf Association and the PGA Tour before joining the team. His reporting confirms that the trick was not about power, but about a refined sense of touch and rhythm.

The technique involved a deliberate approach to the stroke that many amateurs overlook. Instead of trying to muscle the ball, Ballesteros relied on a smooth pendulum motion that felt natural. This allowed him to trust his read completely. When a player trusts their read, they stop fighting the line and start flowing with it. That is where the speed control comes from. It's a simple concept, but executing it under pressure requires years of practice. Ballesteros spent those years perfecting the art of the lag putt. He understood that getting close was more important than making the hole every time. This mindset shifted the entire game for him.

The relevance of Ballesteros' method remains strong in the modern game. Even with advanced technology and laser readings, the human element on the greens cannot be replaced. Players today still struggle with speed control, often leaving putts short or long. The core issue is usually a lack of feel, which is exactly what Ballesteros cultivated. His trick forced him to slow down and focus on the quality of the stroke rather than the result. This is a lesson that applies to any golfer, from the weekend hacker to the Tour professional. By adopting a similar mindset, players can lower their scores without changing their equipment. The mental shift is often the biggest hurdle.

Experts agree that feel is the hardest skill to teach. You can't measure it with a launch monitor. It comes from repetition and confidence. Ballesteros built that confidence through his unique routine. He treated every putt as a test of his own patience and rhythm. This approach allowed him to handle the most stressful situations on the biggest stages. The trick wasn't a secret device or a strange grip change. It was a mental discipline that translated into physical execution. That's why it still resonates with golfers decades after his passing. The fundamentals of speed control haven't changed, even if the courses have.

The next step for golfers interested in this style is to practice the feel, not just the mechanics. Zephyr Melton's reporting on Golf.com serves as a reminder that the greatest players often had the simplest solutions.

articles.title: Joining the Miami Heat is a 'match made in heaven' for Klay Thompson
articles.summary: Klay Thompson seems to have found the perfect fit for him in Miami.
articles.body:
Joining the Miami Heat is a 'match made in heaven' for Klay Thompson originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here .

After years of struggles, the Miami Heat have finally gotten serious with their roster construction. They sent the Milwaukee Bucks a significant trade package to acquire superstar forward Giannis Antetokounmpo . Since the trade involved a lot of players going away, they need more reinforcements.

One of those reinforcements has finally arrived in the form of four-time champion Klay Thompson . He was a star player on the dominant Golden State Warriors alongside Stephen Curry and Draymond Green , who won four titles together.

Klay Thompson believes he found the perfect match with the Miami Heat

The 2026-27 NBA season is set for a blockbuster campaign for a lot of teams, especially in the Eastern Conference. Miami is just one of the teams that have improved their roster, as this also includes the superteam the Philadelphia 76ers are rolling out with the addition of Jaylen Brown and LeBron James .

The Heat have received considerable attention, but it is not on the same level as the 76ers . It can work in the Heat's favor because they can surprise a lot of people, especially with how people spoke about their lack of perimeter shooting. Now, they have one of the greatest shooters of all time in Thompson.

MORE: The reason why Klay Thompson chose to sign with the Heat amid all the offers

As a four-time champion, Thompson knows how to win. Now that he is on the Heat, it seems this is the perfect fit for him. He was unhappy with his chances of winning with the Dallas Mavericks , especially since he thought Luka Doncic would be there for the long term. Now, he is on the Heat looking to win another one.

"I just missed out on the postseason. I hate watching from home. You get FOMO watching all your coworkers just getting to chase their dreams, and it's not fun not making the playoffs. That's all I want to do these next couple years. Have a chance to make a deep postseason run," Thompson said about the Heat being the perfect match in his interview with Brendan Tobin .

"So excited to be in Miami. They're a very demanding organization, but I love being in that ultra-competitive atmosphere, and this was a match made in heaven."

Playing for the Heat comes with extra pressure for most players. However, that is not the case for Thompson because he is quite familiar with the responsibilities he has in Miami. He managed to win four titles in the past, this time, he wants to contribute to win his fifth and help the Heat succeed again.
